Content covers: the chronology of the fifty-two years of Jerusalem's desolation (Zedekiah's exile to Cyrus's decree) and the gematria proof that 'behemah' equals fifty-two, tied to Daniel's 'he strengthened a covenant for the many' and Rabbi Yochanan's covenant-language derivation (l01, l09, l13, vilna 1-11); the story of the priest who discovered the Ark's hiding place by noticing an anomalous pavement tile, and the two blemished priests whose axe fell and ignited a fire while checking wood for worms (l21, l25, vilna 12-19); the cheruvim's visible-yet-not-visible projection through the parochet, compared to a woman's form, with the amah-width screen wall's doorway placement in the First Temple (l27, l31, vilna 19-25); the intertwined cheruvim shown to pilgrims at the festivals as a sign of divine love, cited via Uktzin and Beitza 7a for the meaning of 'attached' (l32, vilna 26-32); the Levites' prohibition on witnessing the Ark's dismantling before it was fully covered, and Rav Nachman's bride analogy for Israel's relationship with the Divine Presence before and after the exile (l35, l36, l38, vilna 32-46); the identity question over which cheruvim were shown (not Solomon's separate pair by the Ark, but the parochet's own), and the count of thirteen curtains in the Second Temple corresponding to the courtyard gates and inner sanctuary (l40, l42, vilna 46-59); and the parallel claim that the First Temple's curtains occupied the same positions, closing with Rav Acha bar Yaakov's view that the Second Temple's cheruvim were only decorative images, not three-dimensional forms (l44, vilna 59-61).
